title: "Real-checkpoint media-tower LoRA — change, control, round-trip, and the corrupt-row contract"
---

```{python}
# | echo: false
import jammi
import jammi_cookbook
```

**Recipe:** `fine_tune(method="lora", task=...)` on `[gpu]` against REAL checkpoints
· `infer` · `describe_model` — the SAME shipped Python surface the
`image_search`/`audio_search` recipes drive, never the internal `jammi-bench`
harness · **Theory:** LoRA — a frozen base weight plus a trainable low-rank update
[@hu2022lora] — injected into OpenCLIP's shared vision/text `ResidualAttentionBlock`
[@radford2021clip] and into CLAP's HTSAT-Swin audio tower [@wu2023clap] · **Rail:**
measurement (a real GPU fine-tune of each of three towers, its invariants read back
through the public surface, frozen once and reasserted here).

Every earlier fine-tuning chapter in this book trains a **text** encoder
(ModernBERT). This one is the media front end's own proof: the SAME `fine_tune`
verb, pointed at REAL OpenCLIP ViT-B-32 (vision **and** text towers — `task=`
alone selects which) and REAL CLAP HTSAT (the audio tower) checkpoints, on real
GPU hardware, exercising the `target_modules` LoRA-site selectors the
`image_search`/`audio_search` recipes introduced for these architectures. The
heavy work ran **once**, on a GPU `jammi-server`; this chapter reads that
committed cache and asserts a measured verdict against `golden_metrics.json`,
never recomputing upstream.

## Provenance, checked before anything else

No sha is exposed anywhere on the shipped surface for the engine commit this
cache was emitted against: `get_server_info()` carries `version` / `features` /
`storage_backends` / `services` only, and the `jammi-ai` client wheel carries a
declared `version`, same story — neither carries a build sha. The finest-grained
identity the shipped surface exposes is the declared VERSION, so that is what
gets checked here, against the CURRENTLY INSTALLED client — the same pattern
Chapter 14 uses for `usearch.__version__` before touching its frozen index.

```{python}
from jammi_cookbook import contracts

record = contracts.load_artifact("media_tower.record")
provenance = record["provenance"]

assert jammi.__version__ == provenance["installed_client_version"], (
    f"installed jammi {jammi.__version__} != the {provenance['installed_client_version']} "
    "this cache was emitted against — a stale cache under a different engine build."
)
print(f"engine version:          {record['engine_version']}")
print(f"installed client:        {jammi.__version__}  (matches)")
print(f"box:                     {provenance['hostname']} / {provenance['gpu_name']} "
      f"(device {provenance['device']})")
print(f"vision/text checkpoint:  {record['vision_checkpoint']}")
print(f"  sha256:                {provenance['vision_checkpoint_sha256']}")
print(f"audio checkpoint:        {record['audio_checkpoint']}")
print(f"  sha256:                {provenance['audio_checkpoint_sha256']}")
print(f"rows per modality:       {record['rows_per_modality']}")
```

Each checkpoint's sha256 above is computed by THIS chapter's emit script,
directly over the checkpoint directory's file bytes, independent of the
engine's own internal per-model digest (`compute_model_content_digest` in
`crates/jammi-ai/src/model/backend/candle.rs`) — that routine never crosses
`describe_model`, the wire proto, or the CLI, so there is no shipped-surface way
to read a registered model's content digest today (`provenance
["content_digest_via_shipped_surface"]` records that fact rather than silently
working around it).

## Five things worth measuring, not one

A recipe that shows "the tuned vector differs from the base vector" is teaching
one fact. This chapter measures five, because each closes a gap the others leave
open:

1. **Change, not improvement.** The adapter must move the served embedding.
   Direction and quality are not claimed — a synthetic, generic triplet corpus
   carries no semantic ground truth — only that training changed something real,
   past a floor and tolerance DERIVED from this cache's own measurements (below),
   never a hand-picked literal.
2. **The same-input control.** A change could, in principle, be inference
   noise rather than a real parameter delta. The control rules that out: the
   SAME probe input, run through the SAME (base) checkpoint **twice**, in two
   independent calls — and it is what derives the change-must-exceed floor
   below.
3. **The round trip — a REAL process restart.** A LoRA delta that trains but is
   silently dropped at serve time is the exact defect the recipes' own comments
   warn about. This chapter's emit script closes the connection that trained the
   adapter, TERMINATES the `jammi-server` OS process, and starts a FRESH one
   against the SAME on-disk catalog before re-deriving the tuned vector — a
   reconnect to the still-running process would only prove the process-local
   cache kept the adapter warm.
4. **Cross-tower selectivity.** OpenCLIP's vision and text towers share one
   checkpoint and one LoRA-site vocabulary; `task=` is supposed to scope a
   fine-tune's trainable sites to ONE tower. A fixed probe through the OTHER,
   untouched tower must be bit-identical to base.
5. **The corrupt-row contract, in both input arms.** The doc's Error-handling
   table covers both an inline-`Binary` column and a `Utf8` (path) column; this
   chapter measures both, on both media types.

## The three towers, measured side by side

`task=` is the only thing that changes which tower of the SAME OpenCLIP
checkpoint gets adapted (`image_embedding` -> vision, `text_embedding` -> the
CLIP text tower); the CLAP checkpoint carries a separate `audio_embedding`
tower. Every tower's `target_modules` names REAL sites on that tower's own
architecture (`in_proj`/`c_fc` on OpenCLIP's shared attention block;
`query`/`value`/`linear1` on HTSAT-Swin) — the same selector vocabulary the
`image_search`/`audio_search` recipes document.

```{python}
towers = record["towers"]
print(f"{'tower':<8}{'task':<18}{'target_modules'}")
for name, t in towers.items():
    print(f"{name:<8}{t['task']:<18}{t['target_modules']}")
```

### 1 — Change vs. base, at a DERIVED tolerance and floor

Each tower's LoRA adapter was trained **twice**, independently (`REPEATS = 2` in
the emit script). The observed spread between those two runs is what derives
this metric's tolerance; the same-input control (measured next) is what derives
the floor a real change must clear — neither is a hand-picked literal.

```{python}
for name, t in towers.items():
    diff = t["change_vs_base_max_abs_diff"]
    td = t["tolerance_derivation"]
    contracts.assert_close(f"media_tower.{name}.change_vs_base_max_abs_diff", diff)
    assert diff > td["change_floor"], (
        f"{name}: the LoRA adapter should change the served embedding past its "
        f"derived floor — max|Δ| = {diff:.6f} <= floor {td['change_floor']:.6g} "
        "(adapter trained but not applied at serve time?)"
    )
    print(f"  {name:<6} change max|Δ| = {diff:.6f}  "
          f"(tol={td['change_tol']:.4g}=k{td['spread_multiplier_k']:g}·spread, "
          f"floor={td['change_floor']:.4g}=k{td['control_floor_multiplier_k']:g}·control)")
```

### 2 — The same-input control

Two independent `infer` calls through the SAME (base) checkpoint, over the
SAME probe input, on each of the two independent training runs above.

```{python}
for name, t in towers.items():
    diff = t["same_input_control_max_abs_diff"]
    contracts.assert_close(f"media_tower.{name}.same_input_control_max_abs_diff", diff)
    print(f"  {name:<6} control max|Δ| = {diff:.6g}")

for name, t in towers.items():
    change = t["change_vs_base_max_abs_diff"]
    control = t["same_input_control_max_abs_diff"]
    assert control < change, (
        f"{name}: the same-input control ({control:.6g}) is not smaller than "
        f"the change vs. base ({change:.6g}) — the measured change is not "
        f"distinguishable from noise"
    )
print("every tower's control diff is strictly below its own change-vs-base signal ✓")
```

### 3 — The round trip: train → save → a REAL process restart → serve

The emit script closes the connection that trained each tower's adapter,
terminates the `jammi-server` OS process, and starts a brand-new one against
the SAME `artifact_dir` before re-deriving the tuned vector. The record carries
the OS pid before and after, so the restart is auditable, not merely claimed.

A round-trip diff is not noisy the way change-vs-base is: either the adapter
survived the restart bit-for-bit or persistence is broken, so this asserts a
tight, HARDCODED ceiling — never merely the golden, which would happily commit
(and then trivially match) a broken measurement.

```{python}
for name, t in towers.items():
    diff = t["round_trip_max_abs_diff"]
    rt = t["round_trip"]
    assert diff < 1e-5, (
        f"{name}: round-trip max|Δ| = {diff:.6f} is not near zero — the "
        "adapter did not survive a real process restart intact"
    )
    contracts.assert_close(f"media_tower.{name}.round_trip_max_abs_diff", diff)
    assert rt["server_restarted"] is True
    assert rt["before"]["pid"] != rt["after"]["pid"], (
        f"{name}: round trip did not cross a real OS process boundary"
    )
    print(f"  {name:<6} round-trip max|Δ| = {diff:.6g}  "
          f"(pid {rt['before']['pid']} -> {rt['after']['pid']})")
print("every tower's adapter round-trips train -> save (catalog) -> a REAL process "
      "restart -> serve ✓")
```

### 4 — Cross-tower selectivity

After tuning the **vision** tower, a fixed probe through the **text** tower
(same checkpoint, untouched) must read bit-identically to base — and
symmetrically after tuning **text**, a probe through **vision** must too.
`max_abs_diff` is asserted **exactly** `0.0`, not within a tolerance: this is a
selectivity property, not a noisy measurement.

```{python}
for name in ("vision", "text"):
    sel = towers[name]["cross_tower_selectivity"]
    contracts.assert_close(f"media_tower.{name}.cross_tower_selectivity_max_abs_diff",
                            sel["max_abs_diff"])
    assert sel["max_abs_diff"] == 0.0, (name, sel)
    print(f"  {name:<6} tuned model probed on {sel['probed_task']:<16} "
          f"max|Δ| vs base = {sel['max_abs_diff']:.1f}  (bit-identical)")
print("tuning one OpenCLIP tower left the other's served embedding untouched ✓")
```

## 5 — The corrupt-row contract, measured in both input arms

`docs/guide/src/generate-image-embeddings.md`'s Error-handling table documents
two accepted input shapes for a media column — inline `Binary` bytes and `Utf8`
file paths — and the SAME three-row contract for both: a valid row
(`_status="ok"`), a **null** row (`_status="error"`, `"Null or missing ... input"`),
and a **corrupt** (undecodable) row (`_status="error"`, naming the row). This
chapter measures both arms, on both media types, and checks the error message's
OWN named row index against the row's actual Arrow position — not a substring
match.

```{python}
for modality, arms in record["corrupt_rows"].items():
    for mode, corrupt in arms.items():
        print(f"\n--- {modality} / {mode} ---")
        print(f"  good row still ok:  {corrupt['good_row_still_ok']}")
        print(f"  null row:           {corrupt['null_row']}")
        print(f"  corrupt row:        {corrupt['corrupt_row']}")

        assert corrupt["good_row_still_ok"], (
            f"{modality}/{mode}: a null/corrupt row in the SAME batch must not "
            f"fail the other, valid row"
        )
        assert corrupt["null_row"]["status"] == "error", corrupt["null_row"]
        assert "null" in corrupt["null_row"]["error"].lower(), corrupt["null_row"]

        # The measured fact: a corrupt (undecodable) row is a per-row
        # `_status="error"` outcome, alongside the good row — the whole `infer`
        # call does NOT raise — and the row index NAMED in its own error
        # message matches the row's actual Arrow position in the batch.
        assert corrupt["corrupt_row"]["status"] == "error", corrupt["corrupt_row"]
        assert corrupt["corrupt_row"]["row_index_matches_arrow_position"], (
            f"{modality}/{mode}: message row index "
            f"{corrupt['corrupt_row']['row_index_in_message']} does not match this "
            "row's actual Arrow position"
        )
```

A genuinely missing/unreadable path (as opposed to an existing, undecodable
file) is a different, column-level failure — `arrow_to_images`/`arrow_to_audio`
raise a whole-call `Err` for that case by design, since resolving a path to
bytes happens before the per-row decode stage. This chapter's path arm uses an
existing file with undecodable bytes, so it measures the per-row contract the
doc table describes, not that column-level case.

## Bridge note

> **The first real-checkpoint chapter in the fine-tuning line.** Every earlier
> `fine_tune` chapter in this book trains a small, hermetic text encoder; this
> one is the media front end's own proof, on real OpenCLIP and real CLAP
> checkpoints, through the identical public surface. The invariants this
> chapter measures generalize past media: change-vs-base is the adapter's
> reason to exist, the same-input control is what makes that change
> interpretable and derives the floor it must clear, the round trip through a
> real process restart is what makes "saved" mean something a new OS process
> can observe, cross-tower selectivity is what proves `task=` actually scoped
> the adapter, and the corrupt-row measurement — in both input arms — proves a
> per-row contract against the branch it describes, with the message's own row
> index checked, not merely searched for.
